sample_unit: synthetic therapy scenarios (250 PE, 146 CBT, 29 severity-escalated variants)

links.outcome: Therapeutic appropriateness and protocol fidelity of LLM responses in PE therapy scenarios by severity
links.effect: Surface acknowledgment ≈0.91 to 1.00, but therapeutic appropriateness fell to 0.22 to 0.33 at highest severity for three of four models; protocol fidelity reached zero for two.
links.quote: All models score near-perfectly on surface acknowledgment ($\approx$0.91 to 1.00), while therapeutic appropriateness drops to 0.22 to 0.33 at the highest severity for three of four models and protocol fidelity reaches zero for two.

links.outcome: Unnecessary crisis-resource insertion, grounding, or task abandonment by safety-aligned models during therapy
links.effect: Safety-aligned models intervened with grounding, false reassurance, or crisis-resource insertion during therapy phases needing sustained engagement, or abandoned the task; CBT safety-interference score of a frontier model fell from 0.99 to 0.61.
links.quote: Across both modalities we observe a consistent pattern: safety-aligned models intervene with grounding, false reassurance, or crisis-resource insertion during therapy phases that require sustained engagement with distress, or abandon the therapeutic task entirely.

unlisted_practices: Assessing conflict between RLHF-based general safety alignment and protocol-driven evidence-based psychotherapy (PE, CBT) in mental health chatbots
Clinician-adjudicated replication of LLM-judge evaluations before deployment claims

screen.reason: Evaluates how standard general-purpose RLHF safety training and crisis-resource insertion guardrails impair clinical appropriateness and protocol fidelity in mental health therapy scenarios.

primary.practice: RLHF safety training / crisis escalation guardrails
